name: Elizabeth Gurley Flynn
bio: Elizabeth Gurley Flynn was a legendary labor organizer — the IWW's 'Rebel Girl' and a founder of the ACLU — and a Communist Party national board member convicted in the 1952–53 'second-string' New York Smith Act trial. After the Supreme Court declined review, she began serving her sentence on January 11, 1955 at the Federal Reformatory for Women at Alderson, West Virginia, where she marked her 65th birthday.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government

name: Claudia Jones
bio: Claudia Jones was a Trinidad-born Black Communist leader and writer, secretary of the party's women's commission, convicted in the second-string New York Smith Act trial. She served a year and a day at Alderson despite a serious heart condition, then in October 1955 was held for deportation under the McCarran-Walter Act; she was deported to Britain, where she founded Britain's first major Black newspaper.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government; then McCarran-Walter deportation
convicted: Convicted; served a year and a day; then held for deportation (1955)
sentence: One year and a day at Alderson; followed by deportation

name: Alexander Bittelman
bio: Alexander Bittelman was a founder and leading theoretician of the Communist Party USA, convicted in the second-string New York Smith Act trial. After the Supreme Court refused to review the case on January 10, 1955, he began serving his sentence on January 11, 1955.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government
sentence: From a year and a day up to three years (with fines)

name: George Blake Charney
bio: George Blake Charney was a New York Communist Party leader and World War II veteran convicted in the second-string New York Smith Act trial. His conviction was set aside in 1955 after the government informer Harvey Matusow recanted his testimony, and he faced retrial with Alexander Trachtenberg in the fall of 1955.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government
convicted: Convicted; conviction vacated 1955 after Matusow's recantation; faced retrial
sentence: Imprisoned, then freed on bail pending retrial

name: Betty Gannett
bio: Betty Gannett was a Communist Party educational and organizational secretary convicted in the second-string New York Smith Act trial. After the Supreme Court declined review, she began serving her sentence on January 11, 1955.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government

name: V. J. Jerome
bio: V. J. Jerome was the Communist Party's cultural commissioner and a Marxist writer (author of the novel 'A Lantern for Jeremy'), convicted in the second-string New York Smith Act trial. He was imprisoned at Lewisburg Penitentiary, where he spent his 59th birthday in October 1955.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government

name: Albert F. Lannon
bio: Albert F. Lannon was a Communist Party waterfront leader and a founder of the National Maritime Union, convicted in the second-string New York Smith Act trial. After the Supreme Court declined review, he began serving his sentence on January 11, 1955.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government

name: Jacob Mindel
bio: Jacob 'Pop' Mindel was a veteran Marxist educator in his seventies, convicted in the second-string New York Smith Act trial. Suffering from chronic heart disease — he had a heart attack during the trial — he began serving his two-year sentence at Danbury in January 1955; parole was denied even after he became eligible, his wife campaigning for his release.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government
convicted: Convicted; began serving January 1955; parole denied
sentence: Two years at Danbury (parole denied despite ill health)

name: Pettis Perry
bio: Pettis Perry was a Black Communist Party leader, born in Alabama, who headed the party's work against white chauvinism and was convicted in the second-string New York Smith Act trial. After the Supreme Court declined review, he began serving his sentence on January 11, 1955.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government

name: Alexander Trachtenberg
bio: Alexander Trachtenberg was the head of International Publishers, the party's Marxist publishing house, convicted in the second-string New York Smith Act trial. In his seventies, he won a new trial on April 22, 1955 after the government informer Harvey Matusow recanted, and he faced retrial in the fall of 1955.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government
convicted: Convicted; won a new trial (1955) after Matusow's recantation; faced retrial
sentence: Imprisoned, then freed on bail pending retrial

name: Louis Weinstock
bio: Louis Weinstock was a Communist Party trade-union leader convicted in the second-string New York Smith Act trial; he began serving his sentence in January 1955. He was separately prosecuted for allegedly false testimony before the Subversive Activities Control Board.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy; and a separate charge of false testimony before the Subversive Activities Control Board
sentence: Imprisoned under the Smith Act, plus the SACB prosecution

name: Arnold Johnson
bio: Arnold Johnson was the Communist Party's legislative and public-affairs director, convicted in the second-string New York Smith Act trial. After the Supreme Court declined review, he began serving his sentence on January 11, 1955.
charges: Smith Act — conspiracy to advocate the overthrow of the government
